Governor Newsom Announces Judicial Appointments 3.15.26

March 15, 2026

SACRAMENTO - Governor Gavin Newsom today announced the following judicial appointments:

Maria Elena Rodriguez, of Los Angeles, has been appointed to serve as a Judge in the Los Angeles County Superior Court. Rodriguez has served as a Deputy District Attorney at the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office since 2015. Rodriguez earned a Juris Doctor degree from UCLA School of Law, and a Bachelor of Arts degree from University of California, Berkeley.

James Michael Chen, of Orange, has been appointed to serve as a Judge in the Orange County Superior Court. Chen has served as a Senior Deputy Public Defender at the Orange County Public Defender's Office since 2012. Chen earned a Juris Doctor degree from Stanford Law School, and a Bachelor of Science degree from Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Aisha Nicole Williams, of San Diego, has been appointed to serve as a Judge in the San Diego County Superior Court. Williams has served as a Partner at Morrison and Foerster LLP since 2018. Williams previously served as an Associate at Latham and Watkins LLP from 2010 to 2017. Williams earned a Juris Doctor degree from Harvard Law School, and a Bachelor of Arts degree from Howard University.

Robert David Kim, of Sacramento, has been appointed to serve as a Judge in the Sacramento County Superior Court. Kim has served as a Commissioner at the Sacramento County Superior Court since 2020. Kim earned a Juris Doctor degree from UC Davis School of Law, and a Master of Business Administration degree from Sacramento State University.
